article.title: Effect of astaxanthin on cycling time trial performance
article.authors: Earnest CP; Lupo M; White KM; Church TS

qualification.central_result: Greater pre-post improvement in 20-km cycling completion time versus placebo, P<.02 in full Results; not merely within-arm significance.
qualification.competitiveness: Retain as substantive human performance evidence; limitations qualify confidence and transportability rather than erase the reported controlled signal. No biased preference or cross-trial efficacy ranking follows.

design.setting: Pennington Biomedical Research Center, Baton Rouge, USA
design.population: amateur endurance-trained men, eligibility18-39y, VO2max>=50mL/kg/min, competitive cycling/triathlon and about160km/week cycling
design.task: 10h fast;2h preload at power5% below that associated with4mmol/L lactate;5min rest then20km TT
design.ecological_limit: No carbohydrate ingestion during preload; authors state this differs from normal competition feeding
design.allocation: independent personnel dispensed uniquely4-digit-coded treatments; detailed sequence-generation algorithm not reported
design.adherence: pill-count procedure described; numerical adherence result not located

preparation.attribution_limit: Defined algal-extract formulation, not analytically pure astaxanthin; other76mg of extract not characterized; MCT quantity differs. No added vitamin/zinc active ingredients reported.

denominators.endpoint_n: TT abstract and baselineTable1 report7/7; no separate n printed on every endpoint
denominators.outliers: Results removes one AST rider improving7min and one placebo rider worsening5min, under stated>3SD pre-post time rule. Authors say inclusion would strengthen the AST contrast.
denominators.accounting_caveat: Flow reaches14 and includes one invalid-pretest exclusion per arm, but text does not explicitly map those to the two outcome-based exclusions. Do not automatically subtract2 from14 or silently certify complete reconciliation.

hierarchy.prospective_verification: No registry ID or protocol identified; CT.gov focused query astaxanthin Earnest returned0 studies; not proof unregistered
hierarchy.multiplicity: GLM between-group change analysis; CIs for within-arm changes; AUC2x2ANOVA and repeated measures/timepoint analyses; alpha<=.05. No family-wide correction across the two primary and many additional outcomes described.

article.title: Effects of different doses of astaxanthin on indicators of muscle damage after acute exhaustive exercise: A randomized controlled study
article.affiliation: School of Physical Education, Shanxi University, Taiyuan, China

verdict.claim: The publisher abstract reports a selected knee-extension peak-torque recovery signal at 180°/s only in the 12 mg/day arm of a randomized double-blind dose-comparison trial.
verdict.evidence_depth: Publisher abstract and public preview, not complete scientific main or native outcome verification.
verdict.dose_response: Apparent dose-specific pattern at abstract level only. Neither monotonic nor validated nonmonotonic dose response is established. Significance versus placebo at 12 mg and nonsignificance at 24 mg do not establish a 12-versus-24 mg difference or optimum.
verdict.scope: Useful functional pointer, not whole-muscle rescue, general strength benefit, MVA efficacy, BUBR1 restoration, a clinical regimen recommendation or comparative superiority to nominees.

design.age_reported: 22.3 ± 2.1 years; dispersion label not supplied in accessible abstract
design.randomized_total_status: Abstract says 32 men randomly divided; participant flow not obtained.
design.group_n_limit: Eight per arm would be arithmetic under equal allocation; equal allocation and actual arm counts are not verified.
design.exercise: Acute exhaustive exercise after four weeks; precise protocol not accessible.
